text.p: Brisbane-based Morgan Stockbroking Ltd said it was recommending QBE Insurance Group Ltd as a buy, reflecting the leading Australian insurer's financial strength, diversification and market positioning.
"We continue to rate it a buy for long-term investors. It is an essential component of any blue chip portfolio," Morgan analyst Nicole Ferro said in a research report.
"QBE trades at a premium to other listed insurance companies which reflects its financial strength, diversification and market positioning," Ferro said.
She said QBE now had a strong and growing presence in key Asian markets with its core strengths seen as a geographic spread of businesses and a diversified product mix.

The key factors driving QBE's profit growth in the medium term were the strong international operations, a solid outlook for the investment portfolio and an ongoing objective to cut costs, Ferro said.
"QBE expects double digit growth from all divisions this year," she said.
Ferro forecast a net profit for QBE of A$155 million in the current year to June 30, 1997, up from A$147.3 million in 1995/96.
The forecast net profit would translate into earnings per share of 53.1 cents compared with last year's 52.8 cents.
"With a payout ratio of around 50 percent, the company is expected to pay dividends totalling 27 cents per share (26 cents in 1995/96), partially franked," Ferro said.
QBE had reported impressive rates of growth over the past 10 years, averaging 22 percent per annum compound, Ferro said.

The insurer could find it difficult to meet these levels of past performance in the future mainly due to lower inflation, a more competitive business environment and a larger capital base, Ferro said.
"Nonetheless, strong management of both claims and expenses backed by a highly profitable and expanding international book will provide the impetus for future profit growth," she said.
QBE shares closed five cents higher at A$6.88 on Tuesday.
